name: Jerez
terms: Denominación de Origen, Spain's main quality tier.
Young wine, sold with little or no aging. Some see a few months in oak.
The driest and palest sherries, aged under a layer of flor yeast that keeps air away. Manzanilla is the same style aged entirely in Sanlúcar de Barrameda.
Aged first under flor, then exposed to air. Darker than a fino, lighter than an oloroso.
Fortified to at least 17%, so no flor grows and it ages with air. Darker and richer, and naturally dry.
Begins like an amontillado, then turns toward the character of an oloroso once its flor dies.
Made from dried Pedro Ximénez grapes. Intensely sweet, dark brown or black.
Sweetened sherries made by blending. Cream sherry usually blends oloroso with Pedro Ximénez.
keyfacts: Palomino is the base of almost all sherry, and Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel are used for sweet wines.
The best vineyards are on albariza, an almost white soil that keeps moisture through the hot summer and suits Palomino best.
Fino and Manzanilla age under a layer of flor, while oloroso ages only oxidatively once the initial flor has gone.
Amontillado is first aged under flor and then exposed to oxygen, which makes it darker than a fino but lighter than an oloroso.
In the solera system, wine moves through several tiers of barrels, so most sherry carries no vintage, and VOS and VORS mean at least 20 and 30 years average age.

notes: Sherry is made mainly from Palomino, and because it is fortified after fermentation, most sherry is dry.
Fino and Manzanilla are light, very dry and delicate, while Amontillado and Oloroso are darker and heavier from aging with air.
Amontillado is dry and nutty, and Oloroso is full bodied, complex and round.
Palo Cortado combines the nose of Amontillado with the depth and body of Oloroso.
Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel, from dried grapes, are intensely sweet, and Cream sherry is usually Oloroso sweetened with Pedro Ximénez.

blurb.text: The DO for sherry, made from white grapes grown around Jerez de la Frontera in Andalusia. Palomino makes styles from light fino to darker, oxidized amontillado and oloroso. Manzanilla, from Sanlúcar de Barrameda, has its own DO. Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel make sweet dessert sherries.
